problem: Identify which VLA finetuning design decisions improve task performance and inference efficiency when adapting a pretrained model to robot manipulation.
contribution: OpenVLA-OFT studies parallel decoding, action chunks, continuous action objectives and optional FiLM language conditioning with controlled alternatives to the original autoregressive discrete OpenVLA recipe.
algorithm: Insert empty action embeddings and replace causal action decoding with bidirectional attention to predict all action entries/chunks in one forward pass. Compare L1 regression and diffusion heads under LoRA finetuning; add wrist/proprio inputs where specified and FiLM for language-dependent ALOHA tasks.
observations: Condition-dependent: overview image and language; enhanced variants add wrist/multiple images and proprioception. Original versus modified filtered demonstration datasets are separated in the source table.
actions: Continuous chunks, LIBERO7D with chunk8; ALOHA14D with chunk25. Action-generation throughput counts entries across a chunk and differs from fresh observation-conditioned inference frequency.
embodiment_and_data: OpenVLA7B base; each LIBERO suite500demonstrations/10tasks, finetuned independently. Physical ALOHA studies use bimanual/multiview inputs; base pretraining did not include that bimanual configuration.
experiments: LIBERO500evaluation episodes per suite (10tasks×50), plus ALOHA task/language-following comparisons. Speed tables average100queries on A100; different policy/runtime implementations remain a comparison caveat.
baselines: Original OpenVLA, PD/chunk/L1/diffusion ablations, ACT, Diffusion Policy, Octo, pi0, RDT-1B, MDT and Seer. Many quality scores come from published papers with differing inputs/data; pi0 uses optimized JAX while others are PyTorch.

quantitative_result.value: Enhanced filtered-input OpenVLA-OFT averages97.1% LIBERO success; same family with single-image inputs95.3%, unfiltered enhanced94.5%, showing protocol dependence. ALOHA throughput77.9Hz at0.321s latency for25-action chunks on A100; this is not77.9fresh-feedback decisions/s.

limitations: Offline imitation from expert data, not demonstrated online improvement. Language grounding can collapse without FiLM despite competent motion; extra inputs/data filters affect comparisons. Bimanual runtime and quality cannot be transferred from A100 to NX without execution evidence.
code_and_license: Primary implementation design/evaluation read; repository revision and separate code/base-model licensing not inspected here. No local OFT implementation is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: Useful adaptation baseline if the base model is actually available and affordable. Log chunk size, end-to-end latency, freshness and processor semantics; compare ACT's compact genuine architecture before selecting a larger model on reported throughput alone.
